subject: SIR and the struck-off names
alt: Cartoon: a stout leader in a saffron gamchha raises a finger at a thin old man in dhoti-kurta and says that if your name has been cut in SIR it may be your own fault: perhaps you are dead or a foreign national.
chutki: This picture by Rajendra Dhodapkar explains the new rule of our times: the fault always lies with the one who has the fewest papers. Look at the finger of the gentleman in the gamchha: it does not ask a question, it pronounces a verdict. The thinner the old man standing before him, the thinner his citizenship has been made.

The real fun of the cartoon is in its logic. If the name is cut, only two things are possible: either you are dead, or you are a foreigner. The third possibility, that the maker of the list made a mistake, cannot even be thought of in this democracy. Asking a living man for proof that he is alive: that is today's greatest government miracle.
